_comment: Contract between mann1x/ollama and xollama. See FORK-SYNC.md (mann1x/xollama@dev).
patches[] ORDER IS APPLY ORDER. Merge each as its own --no-ff merge, in this order.
Two branches lack the up- prefix because they are heads of open cross-fork PRs:
renaming such a branch CLOSES the PR (measured 2026-09-21 on #18307). They get the
prefix if and when those PRs close.
status 'fork-only' means there is no upstream PR and none is planned: the patch
is ours to carry and upstream_pr is null. Every other entry is 'open-upstream'.

A patch whose changes cannot exist on the upstream tag gets a stacked up- branch: its row carries depends_on and a base that is the dependency set rather than the tag, the branch is built on the merge of exactly those dependencies AT THEIR MANIFEST SHAS, it is listed after all of them, and it is fork-only. up-response-scope-think-budget is the first.

mlx.layout: From v0.40.9 (#17956) neither MLX archive is self-contained. Linux: ollama-linux-amd64-mlx.tar.zst no longer carries libcublas, libcublasLt, libcudart, libnvrtc(+builtins) or libnvJitLink in lib/ollama/mlx_cuda_v13 (v0.40.6 did); its libraries find them through RPATH $ORIGIN/../cuda_v13, i.e. the main archive's GGML CUDA payload. Windows: ollama-windows-amd64-mlx.zip holds mlx_cuda_v13/{mlx,mlxc,ollama_xgrammar,libopenblas,8 cudnn*}.dll and cuda_v13/{cufft64_12,cusolver64_12,cusparse64_12}.dll; cublas64_13, cublasLt64_13, cudart64_13, nvrtc64_130_0, nvrtc-builtins64_130 and nvJitLink_130_0 come from the main ollama-windows-amd64.zip's lib/ollama/cuda_v13 (listed from upstream's v0.40.9 zip). The MLX payload must be installed over a cuda_v13 that carries those.

patches.title: gemma4: a channel re-opened inside thinking leaks into the reasoning
patches.note: Requested by xollama (#1547). The model writes <|channel> inside an open thinking block when it means to close it or begin another thought; the thinking state passed it through with its channel name, so the reasoning carried a literal '<|channel>thought' (pandorum 2026-10-16, gemma4 v9-agentic, two blocks of one run; once as '<|channel><thought>'). Reproduced by xollama on dev 817123de7 streamed one rune at a time. A re-opened <|channel> before <channel|> and <|tool_call> is now dropped with its name (thought\n, <thought>\n, <thought>, or a bare thought at done) and the block goes on, the next text starting on a new line; a partial <|channel> is held back like the other two tags. The tool-call-in-thinking half is gemma4-toolcall-in-thinking's and is unchanged. Tests in their own file (gemma4_reopened_channel_test.go, whole and rune-by-rune): all 6 fail on the base and pass with the fix; go test ./model/parsers/ passes; golangci-lint --new-from-rev=6bb6f388 0 issues. Integrated into think-budget by cherry-pick -x (36c0592d), clean. Superseded for xollama: gemma4-channel-in-thinking@2d27c61b0, the same fix written against bare upstream with both halves, is not in this manifest.

patches.title: llm: parse llama-server output by line and count a speculative draft's buffers
patches.note: Reported by backup_models (#1764): pandorum v0.40.4-thinkbudget, Qwen3.5 9B Q6_K with an MTP draft fully on an RTX 5080, /api/ps 373 MiB then 905 MiB against 11.8 GB in nvidia-smi. Two faults in upstream's memoryParsingWriter: buffer lines were matched per Write, and a line split across two pipe reads was lost; and the draft context logs the same component/backend/kind as the target, so its KV (512) and compute (172) replaced the target's (2176, 704). Now line-buffered, with buffers logged between 'creating MTP draft context'/'loading draft model' and 'speculative decoding context initialized'/'model loaded' keyed as the draft; a later compute re-reserve whose size the draft holds and the target does not is the draft's. resetLoadAccounting clears the writer too. Replay of the real load at chunk sizes 1..4096 and whole: 10167.88 MiB GPU, = llama-server's own 'projected to use 10167 MiB'; the base gives 0..7991.88. go test ./llm/ passes on the branch and on think-budget. Integrated by cherry-pick -x (b6a9febd), clean.

patches.title: qwen3.5: tell the tool parser the output ended, even on an empty last chunk
patches.note: Reported by xollama (mail 1163, ol-62): qwen3.5:2b, think:false, ended done_reason=stop inside a <tool_call> it never closed; the response had no content and no call. Upstream v0.40.6 already flushes a held call as content in Qwen3CoderParser when told done, but Qwen35Parser passed done only with a content event, so the usual done-only final chunk never reached it. done is now passed once after all events. TestQwen35ParserUnclosedToolCallAtEndIsReturnedAsContent fails on v0.40.6 without it (empty final chunk case).

patches.title: llama: accept generation_prompt on completion requests again
patches.note: 2026-10-23. A llama.cpp patch, so it retires on a LLAMA_CPP_VERSION bump once the pin registers generation_prompt in tools/server/server-schema.cpp again (check: grep -c 'field_str("generation_prompt")' in the fetched tree is 1 without 006). A template that primes thinking ends the prompt with the opening tag; llm/llama_server.go sends that tail as generation_prompt (98d344a7d) and llama-server replays it into the reasoning budget sampler. b11521 registered the field, b11669 dropped it, so from v0.40.6-thinkbudget through v0.40.9-thinkbudget a think_budget on qwen3, gemma4 or any other priming template was echoed in the response and never enforced. Found by the v0.40.9 smoke generation on pandorum and eleven2go (qwen3:4b, budget 64: thinking to num_predict, no answer). Verified: the /completion body Ollama sends, captured off loopback, is inert on b11669 and b11803 and activates, closes at a line boundary and answers on b11803+006; without the field the patched build stays inert. test-reasoning-budget cannot see this: it never goes through the request schema.
